newsitem.title: UK: Tin prices seen rising in 1997 - Rudolf Wolff.
newsitem.headline: Tin prices seen rising in 1997 - Rudolf Wolff.

text.p: World tin prices are forecast to rise this year amid a recovery in global demand and renewed fund interest, brokers Rudolf Wolff & Co said in a report.
Wolff forecast prices to average $6,350 per tonne in 1997, compared to $6,200 last year.

"Whilst we expect the resultant higher prices to encounter increased selling by the Chinese and low cost producers, with a demand/supply deficit forecast for 1997, demand is expected to absorb this overhead supply," analyst Martin Squires said in the special report.
The market is expected to be in a deficit of 3,000 tonnes this year, compared to a deficit of 3,700 in 1996.
Western production is expected to continue rising, but developing world consumption will underpin a growth in demand.

"Consumption is expected to grow by three percent this year, following the disappointing one percent decrease last year when tin, as most metals, suffered from the industry-wide destocking," the report said.
Rising industrial demand for tin is expected in developed countries, while demand for electronics and canning in developing world remains robust.
Tin demand is also seen rising as a more environmentally friendly subsitute for lead and via recovered market share in the drinks can market.
The presence of funds is expected to increase in the tin market as the recovery in industrial production attracts interest to the base metals.
On the charts, tin's downtrend from mid-1995 is losing momentum in recent months and technical indicators are also trending higher, the report said.
Upside targets are $6,130 and $6,175, which if breached signal a continued recovery. Otherwise consolidation around $6,175-$5,680 may be needed.
